Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one isolated modular equipment design reference for a realistic fantasy RPG; this is pre-modeling costume design, NOT a finished fitted 3D model.
Reference 1 is the APPROVED rogue costume design: faithfully preserve its moss-green short folded hood/cowl, faded flax linen, worn reddish-russet leather, ochre waist cloth, muted blue-gray trousers, umber soft boots and hand-repaired old-school dungeon-adventurer character.
References 2 and 3 show the ACTUAL current modular male base mesh from the game, front and side in its fixed rest pose. Use its real adult male body proportions, shoulder width, torso depth, hand/foot sizes and stout calves rather than the slimmer painted hero. Base height 1.90 m. For any sleeves, follow this exact lowered A pose: each upper arm is about 27 degrees out from vertical, elbows nearly straight, hands palms inward/down, never palms forward.
Scene and style: isolated empty wearable items on clean uniform warm very light gray background. Crisp realistic hand-painted 3D-production concept rendering, materials as in reference 1, soft even studio light, restrained worn detail with readable construction. NO human body, skin, dummy, mannequin, face, skeleton, floor scene, text, captions, dimensions, arrows, labels, watermarks or other equipment not specifically requested. Garments keep their natural worn 3D volume with hollow openings, not flat patterns. Keep ample margins. Match the approved design, adapting construction only for clean modular assembly. No modern zippers, tactical hardware, denim jeans detailing, long coat, skirt, long cape or dangling strips crossing joints.
Requested item: the COMPLETE UPPER GARMENT as one chest-slot assembly: flax linen rolled-sleeve shirt + short worn reddish-russet leather vest with a tiny leather shoulder cap on wearer's LEFT shoulder + short moss-green cowl with the hood folded DOWN against upper back. These three layers are shown ALREADY worn together, never as loose floating separated garments. No headgear.
Construction: keep the reference's attractive irregular diagonal overlapping leather chest panels, side lacing, visible repaired edging and simple muted metal fasteners; no black crossed chest harness. Shirt collar peeks out, linen sleeves rolled to just below each elbow, leaving most forearm and wrists free. Fit the shoulders and roomy armholes to the actual mannequin. Cowl stays close to collarbones and upper back, ends ABOVE armpit level at the sides, and does not bridge to either upper arm or hang below the chest. Its small shoulder pin fastens to the upper vest. The short vest ends at natural waist; no long tails. The shirt has a SHORT plain continuous tuck-in hem extending only 3 cm below the vest, no belt or sash. Leave this hem unobstructed so it can later tuck inside a separate trouser waistband. Neck and sleeve openings are hollow. No arms, no trousers, no belt, no pouches, no hands or weapons.
Composition: landscape two-view construction sheet of THIS SAME SINGLE UPPER GARMENT, FRONT at left and BACK at right, equal scale, nearly orthographic, matching lowered A-shaped empty sleeves. Entire garment visible in each view. Exact same shoulder cap side and cowl cut in both views: wearer's left shoulder is on viewer RIGHT in front view and viewer LEFT in back view. Back shows folded-down hood resting flat at upper spine, fitted simple leather back below it, and a continuous clean waist hem.

Reinforced patch repairs at both knees, gently roomy thighs fitted to reference mannequin, straight relaxed legs set apart exactly as the mannequin rather than a narrow fashion stance.
Construction: waist follows natural waist on the actual modular body; complete 5 cm tall belt and ochre folded cloth band conceal the eventual shirt hem. Ochre sash tail is tucked back under belt so nothing hangs down across the hip crease. Front central belt buckle leaves a clear 6 cm band above it for the vest overlap. Equipment is restrained: two compact flat brown leather pouches on sides, one flat back-right map/lockpick wallet and a small flat rope coil held by TWO straps at back-left. Keep all pouches shallow, attached entirely to the trouser belt and above the high thigh, well away from groin, knee and swinging hands. Do NOT include a knife, dagger, sheath, key, key ring, tools sticking out or weapon: runtime weapons stay separate. No straps running onto a shirt or torso.
Lower legs taper smoothly into simple tucked ankle cuffs: cuffs narrow only at the final few centimeters, enough to insert 3–4 cm INTO a separate LOW ankle boot. Keep the true mannequin calf thickness above that. Both ankle openings are hollow; no boot folds on trousers, no calf-high gaiters, no cuffs folded OVER shoes.
Composition: one landscape two-view construction sheet, FRONT at left and BACK at right, equal scale, orthographic and fully visible from waistband to ankle hems. Exact consistent pouch placement, belt height, leg length and knee patches across views.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit ONLY the attached rogue trouser FRONT/BACK design sheet to make the waist accessories practical to assemble as one hip-weighted modular equipment part. Keep the exact blue-gray trousers, leg pose, knee patches, ankle cuff geometry, reddish-brown leather pouches, ochre cloth, belt height, two-view layout, material detail and background.
Make these two targeted construction corrections consistently in both views:
1. The ochre cloth MUST have NO dangling scarf end. Tuck the loose end entirely behind the belt, forming a continuous compact folded waistband with a clean lower edge above the groin/hip crease. Remove the hanging pointed yellow fabric in the front view. Preserve the ochre band above and below the belt.
2. In the back view make the rope coil SMALLER and FLATTER, compact against the upper back-left hip and held by TWO short leather keepers, one near the top of coil and one near its bottom. The coil should be shallow, about the size of the flat pouch on the opposite hip, ending above the buttock fold. Nothing dangles or extends outward past the pouches.
Everything else unchanged. Output the same two-view sheet, no text or added objects.

Keep the wrist at top and the four finger tubes pointing down. This should now clearly be the same anatomically RIGHT glove seen from dorsal and palmar directions. Do not swap the panels. Do not mirror the complete image. Preserve all leather, stitching, buckles, proportions, hollow openings, background and positions. No text or added objects.
